title: A Noetherian complete local ring is a Nagata ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is complete, i.e. $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]: the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$ is bijective. Then $R$ is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the domain $R/\mathfrak p$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), statement and proof lines 45754-45777; cited in the remarks after Definition Tag 032X (line 45799) and used in the proof of Lemma Tag 032Y (4), line 45869

proof.text: *Reduction to complete local domains.* By [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] we must show that $R$ is Noetherian, which is a hypothesis, and that $R/\mathfrak p$ is N-2 for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$. Fix $\mathfrak p$; it is a proper ideal, so by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient] the ring $R/\mathfrak p$ is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p$ which is $(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p)$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; it is an integral domain because $\mathfrak p$ is prime. Hence it suffices to prove: (*) every Noetherian local domain $(D,\mathfrak n)$ which is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), proof, lines 45759-45777, first paragraph: 'Then R/p is also a complete local Noetherian ring, see Lemma quotient-complete-local (0325). Hence it suffices to show that a Noetherian complete local domain R is N-2.'

proof.text: *Reduction to power series rings.* Let $(D,\mathfrak n)$ be as in (*). By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular] there is a subring $D_0\subseteq D$ such that $D$ is a finitely generated $D_0$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $D_0$ is isomorphic, as a ring, to $\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] for some $d\ge0$, where $\Lambda_0$ is either a field or a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. $D_0$ is an integral domain, being a subring of $D$. Suppose we know (**): for $\Lambda_0$ a field or a Cohen ring and every $d\ge0$, the ring $\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ is a Noetherian integral domain which is N-2. Being Noetherian and being N-2 are properties of the abstract ring, preserved by a ring isomorphism $\sigma:\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]\xrightarrow{\sim}D_0$ ($\sigma$ carries ideals and their generators to ideals and generators; it extends to an isomorphism of fraction fields, so for a finite extension $L$ of $\operatorname{Frac}(D_0)$, viewed through $\sigma$ as a finite extension of $\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda_0[[X]])$, the integral closures of the two rings in $L$ coincide as subsets, the monic equations corresponding under $\sigma$, and module generators are the same elements). So $D_0$ is Noetherian and N-2, and [lem-weil-pbc-n2-ascends-finite-domain-extension] applied to $A=D_0\subseteq B=D$ shows that $D$ is N-2. It remains to prove (**). Lean realization: transport N-2 across a ring isomorphism by applying [lem-weil-pbc-n2-ascends-finite-domain-extension] to its induced algebra structure. The map is injective and surjective, and surjectivity makes this algebra finite. This uses the same finite-extension lemma as the final ascent from the power series subring to D.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), proof, lines 45759-45777, first paragraph: 'By Lemmas quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese (032I) and complete-local-Noetherian-domain-finite-over-regular (032D) we reduce to the case R = k[[X_1,...,X_d]] where k is a field or R = Lambda[[X_1,...,X_d]] where Lambda is a Cohen ring.'

proof.text: *Induction on the number of variables.* Let $\Lambda_0$ be any Noetherian integral domain which is N-2. We show by induction on $d\ge0$ that $\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ is a Noetherian integral domain which is N-2. For $d=0$ the ring is $\Lambda_0$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For $d\ge1$, the map $\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]\to(\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_{d-1}]])[[X_d]]$ sending $\sum_Ea_EX^E$ to $\sum_{j\ge0}\bigl(\sum_{E'}a_{(E',j)}X'^{E'}\bigr)X_d^j$ ($E=(E',j)$, $E'\in\mathbf N^{d-1}$) is a bijection, since $\mathbf N^d=\mathbf N^{d-1}\times\mathbf N$, is additive, and is multiplicative because both products have the coefficient $\sum_{E+F=G}a_Eb_F$ at $G=(G',j)$, the inner sum being regrouped by the last coordinate; so it is a ring isomorphism. By induction $\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_{d-1}]]$ is a Noetherian N-2 domain, so by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-n2] its power series ring in $X_d$ is a Noetherian N-2 domain, and by the isomorphism (as in Step 2) so is $\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$. Thus (**) reduces to: a field, and a Cohen ring, is a Noetherian N-2 domain. Lean realization: Mathlib MvPowerSeries.isEmptyEquiv identifies the zero-variable ring with the coefficient ring, and MvPowerSeries.finSuccEquiv identifies the successor ring with PowerSeries of the preceding ring. Their inverses and the isomorphism transport from Step 2 complete the induction. Mathlib supplies Noetherianity of finite-variable power series and NoZeroDivisors.to_isDomain supplies their domain structure.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), proof, lines 45759-45777, second paragraph: 'In the case k[[X_1,...,X_d]] we reduce to the statement that a field is N-2 by Lemma power-series-over-N-2 (032Q)' and 'In the case Lambda[[X_1,...,X_d]] we reduce to the statement that a Cohen ring Lambda is N-2' (the iteration over the d variables, left implicit there)

proof.text: *A field is a Noetherian N-2 domain.* Let $k$ be a field and let $L$ be a finite extension [def-pc-field-extension] of its fraction field. For any fraction field $K$ of $k$, including one in a different universe, compose the inverse of Mathlib FractionRing.algEquiv k k with FractionRing.algEquiv k K to obtain a k-algebra isomorphism from k to K. Thus K is finite over k. Transitivity of finite modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] makes $L$ finite over $k$. Since $k$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], its integral closure in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], a $k$-submodule of $L$, is finite as well. In Lean these are Module.Finite.equiv, Module.Finite.trans, and Module.IsNoetherian.finite. The private helper isN2_field is generalized in place to arbitrary K rather than duplicating the fixed-FractionRing helper in FiniteTypeZDomainNormalizationFinite; importing that module here would close an import cycle. This proves N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] without needing to identify the integral closure with the whole extension.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), proof, lines 45759-45777, second paragraph: 'we reduce to the statement that a field is N-2 by Lemma power-series-over-N-2. This is clear.'

proof.text: *A Cohen ring is a Noetherian N-2 domain.* Let $\Lambda$ be a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]: a discrete valuation ring, in particular a principal ideal domain, whose maximal ideal is $p\Lambda$ and which is $p\Lambda$-adically complete. By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] $\Lambda$ is a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; this is hypothesis (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-tate-n2-complete-principal] for $R=\Lambda$, $x=p$. Since $p\Lambda$ is a maximal ideal, $\Lambda/p\Lambda$ is a field, hence an integral domain which is N-2 by Step 4: hypothesis (2). The $p\Lambda$-adic completeness in [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] is hypothesis (3) ($x^n\Lambda=p^n\Lambda$) [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. So [lem-weil-pbc-tate-n2-complete-principal] shows that $\Lambda$ is N-2, and it is Noetherian and a domain.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), proof, lines 45759-45777, second paragraph: 'Applying Lemma tate-japanese (032P) once more with x = p in Lambda we reduce yet again to the case of a field. Thus we win.'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By Steps 4 and 5, $\Lambda_0$ is a Noetherian N-2 domain when it is a field or a Cohen ring; by Step 3, so is $\Lambda_0[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ for every $d$, which is (**). By Step 2, (*) holds, and by Step 1 every $R/\mathfrak p$ is N-2; with $R$ Noetherian, $R$ is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring].
